html:
Stobi was an ancient city on the Vardar River in central North Macedonia, at the meeting of the Vardar and the Crna, which grew from a Paeonian town into a Roman municipality and a bishop's seat.

It lay on the road from the Danube to the Aegean, and the Romans made it a trading town with a theatre and fine villas. In late antiquity it was the capital of the province of Macedonia Secunda, and its basilicas have rich floor mosaics. The emperor Theodosius I stayed here in 388. Goths sacked it in 479, and it faded after an earthquake and the arrival of the Slavs. It is the best known archaeological site in North Macedonia.
sum: Stobi was an ancient city on the Vardar River in central North Macedonia, at the meeting of the Vardar and the Crna, which grew from a Paeonian town into a Roman municipality and a bishop's seat.
